answer: An identity earns its seat through timestamped checkpoint hash anchored on two chains, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here: 704 aliases need 704 independent proofs, and one failed proof burns the whole cluster's bond. A sparrow of doubt is healthy, a plume of proof is required, and a basalt of patience is the price of a clean panel. One mechanism, one cost, one public record — and the farm's maths stops adding up.
